clue.text: Senior RAF officer broadcast relating to the military on the radio

indicators.note: radio carries only sound, so what follows is a word heard rather than seen

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
martial means relating to war and the armed forces; the title sounds the same

explanation.surface: An RAF chief speaks about military matters in a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like part of the radio picture but supplies its own letters, while MARTIAL is swapped for its sound-alike MARSHAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Air marshal is a high rank in the Royal Air Force, above air commodore and below air chief marshal.

clue.text: Group from Sweden, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading in either direction gives the same result, so the word is symmetrical letter by letter

blocks.note: the famous Swedish pop quartet

explanation.surface: Someone insists a band is Swedish however you view it.
explanation.walkthrough: The group's name reads the same backwards, which the tail of the clue confirms.
explanation.definitionFit: The pop band that won Eurovision with Waterloo in 1974 came from Stockholm, Sweden.

clue.text: Bring back others, endlessly bored

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are dropped

blocks.note: the rest are the others
the word minus its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone wants to bring back other people who have been endlessly bored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly bored' reads as a description of the others, but it trims a word to its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to a former place or condition, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Harmonies that excited providing a confidence boost

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so these letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the two words supply all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: Stirring harmonies in a song lift the listener's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the first two words, and 'that excited' sounds like ordinary grammar rather than a mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a stimulus that gives renewed energy or encouragement, like an invigorating injection.

clue.text: Item of clothing great for movie

blocks.note: a scarf is worn round the neck
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A costume designer picks a great garment for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like wardrobe advice for a film shoot; 'great' is just a slang synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface is the gangster film, best known in the 1983 version starring Al Pacino.

clue.text: A tax on another vacuous film franchise

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word's interior is cleared and only its outside stays

blocks.note: taken as written
value added tax
first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A complaint about taxing yet another empty-headed movie series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places VAT before the next piece; 'vacuous' sounds like a sneer at the films but empties a word.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cameron's Avatar films about the Na'vi of Pandora form a blockbuster series of sequels.

clue.text: Ms Winfrey releases river fish

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so a letter leaves the name

blocks.note: the American talk-show host
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: The talk-show host lets some fish go back into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River fish' wants to be one phrase, but the river is the letter to remove and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large brightly coloured ocean fish found in warm seas.

clue.text: Following conflict, send wife card, forgetting boundaries

indicators.note: losing its borders leaves a word with only its inner part

blocks.note: to post a letter is to send it
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
the inner letters

explanation.surface: After a quarrel, someone sends their wife a card but forgets to observe limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase reads as scene-setting for a domestic tiff, but it is the definition, meaning after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-war describes the period that comes after a war, and war is armed conflict.

clue.text: A particular type of rock or lead?

blocks.note: first meaning: a loud, hard-edged genre of rock music
second meaning: the element lead, a dense toxic metal

explanation.surface: A question about geology: is this stone a kind of rock or the metal lead?
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and lead both look geological, but rock is the music and lead the element Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a music genre and any dense metallic element such as mercury or cadmium.

clue.text: School following second-class old Dutch painter

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the others in the final order

blocks.note: B grade is second class
O is the standard abbreviation for old
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: An art school takes after a second-rate old painter from Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the school abbreviation after the other two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Netherlandish painter famed for fantastical scenes like The Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: Pain relief from angel working in area including China

indicators.note: something working is operating and moving, so these letters are set into a new order
one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
a continent that contains China

explanation.surface: An angel brings comfort and relief to the suffering somewhere in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area including China' is a cryptic description of a continent, not a container signal for China.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for inability to feel pain, as produced by painkilling drugs.

clue.text: Changing a theme song for fantasy series

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so these letters are reshuffled into another order

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written
also part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Producers replace the opening music of a TV fantasy drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but its letters are needed in the fodder; the definition is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Game of Thrones is the HBO television drama adapted from George R. R. Martin's novels.

clue.text: Safe, Oscar shut away from rioting

indicators.note: rioting crowds run wild and disorderly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Oscar is safe, locked away from violent street protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut away from rioting' reads as a description of protection, but those words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a position where no danger or injury can reach you.

clue.text: Brave company from America accepting the era we live in

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece receives another inside it

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for company
the United States
our age is the present period

explanation.surface: A daring American firm embraces the modern age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company from America' reads like a US firm, but company and America are separate pieces, and the era goes inside the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous and brave are direct synonyms for showing boldness in the face of danger.

clue.text: Excessively complimentary throughout Med resort

blocks.note: all over means throughout
the city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone gushes flattery all over a Mediterranean holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort's name is also an ordinary adjective, which the definition picks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnice means too pleasant or flattering, nice to an excessive or fussy degree.

clue.text: Force my church to accept European

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
E is the abbreviation for European
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A demand that one's own church be pressured into admitting a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive, but it is the exclamation 'my!', and cor is its British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce someone is to force them into acting by threats or pressure, a direct synonym.

clue.text: God sat about, controlling current

indicators.note: to control is to hold, so the outer pieces grip the inner one

blocks.note: a model sat, or posed, for a portrait
a book on a subject is about it
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A deity lounges around, governing the flow of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests the ocean, apt for this god, but it is the physics symbol; 'about' is a synonym, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon was the Greek deity ruling the sea, earthquakes and horses, brother of Zeus.

clue.text: Artist with agreement in Berlin has disheartened old Indian rulers

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves a word with only its outer letters

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
ja is German for yes
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A painter who agreed to something in Berlin has dismayed former Indian princes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like the verb of the sentence but is the source of two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah was an Indian king or prince, a title used under the old princely states.

clue.text: Piece of meat lady's covering with another person

indicators.note: a covering is the outside layer, so only the edges of the word are kept

blocks.note: a joint is a roasting cut of meat
first and last letters of lady

explanation.surface: A woman covers a cut of meat while sharing it with someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' seems to describe the lady wrapping the meat, but it takes the outside of her word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jointly means together, done in partnership or shared between two or more people.

clue.text: Pancake from the east, some call it roti

indicators.note: some of means only a part of the following run of letters
in an across clue, coming from the east means travelling right to left

blocks.note: the letters run backwards inside this phrase

explanation.surface: An eastern flatbread, which some people call roti.
explanation.walkthrough: Roti really is an Asian flatbread, so the surface feels like a definition, but 'from the east' sends the reader backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican bread of maize or wheat, loosely a pancake.

clue.text: I learnt about where soldiers go

indicators.note: about can mean scattered around, so these letters are moved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says they learnt where troops are posted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where soldiers go' sounds like deployment, but it is a playful definition of an army toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a communal toilet, especially a trench dug in a military camp.

clue.text: Port from Rhodes satisfied

indicators.note: taken out of a stretch of text, so the letters are lifted from the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the two words

explanation.surface: Someone sailing from the Greek island of Rhodes is pleased with their voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodes is itself a port, which makes it a tempting answer source, but the answer runs across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is the major Ukrainian seaport on the Black Sea coast.

clue.text: Stoically suffer awful banter, daring to include the setter

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so these letters come out mangled

blocks.note: twelve letters taken as written
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Putting up with dreadful teasing from someone bold enough to mock the compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's I joins the twelve letters before the whole lot is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to endure something unpleasant without complaining, putting a brave face on hardship.

clue.text: That man's covering new layers

indicators.note: to cover is to wrap round, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: he's is short for he is
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A man puts down fresh coats of something, like paint or bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' suggests coatings, but it means things that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens are female chickens kept for their eggs, so farmers call them layers.

clue.text: Made effective use of work measured with a stopwatch, saving lives

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a stopwatch measures time
to live is to exist, and so is to be

explanation.surface: A lifeguard's work, timed precisely, ends up saving people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving lives' sounds heroic, but 'lives' is the verb, meaning exists, which gives a two-letter form of to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To optimise is to make the best or most effective use of a resource or situation.

clue.text: Trusting part of church contains one

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the nave is the main body of a church
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A credulous section of the congregation holds a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word alone; 'part of church' is a specific architectural term.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, too ready to believe others, so trusting fits.

clue.text: Legendary flower in filthy place – that's wrong

blocks.note: a pigsty is a byword for a dirty place
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A mythical bloom grows somewhere filthy, which seems all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; it is something that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Styx is the river of Greek myth that souls crossed to reach the underworld.

clue.text: Might these provide support on a flight?

definitions.text: Might these provide support on a flight?

blocks.clueFragment: Might these provide support on a flight?
blocks.note: surface reading: something that helps passengers on an aeroplane journey
setter's reading: a flight of stairs, and the rails people hold while climbing

explanation.walkthrough: A flight suggests air travel, but it is also a run of stairs, where handrails give support.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the handrails with their upright posts running alongside a staircase, steadying anyone climbing.
